rationale: Matthew 12:41 directly carries the entry’s distinctive core: the men of Nineveh as Gentile people who repented and will rise in judgment to condemn those who reject the greater-than-Jonah. The strongest counter is essentially the same core (plain historical-exemplar reading of the Ninevites as condemning witnesses) and does not materially deny it; no supplied detail is explained by the counter that the book core cannot explain. The printed secondary frame “great city of the sea,” however, is a book-method elaboration (sea = peoples; Nineveh as mass of nations) that is only thinly evidenced in the bundle and is not required by the cited verse, so support is CORE_ONLY rather than FULL.
book_core_identification: Nineveh as Gentile people who repent and rise in judgment against those who reject Jesus (the greater than Jonah).
book_secondary_elaborations: A great city of the sea
unsupported_glossary_assertions: A great city of the sea (symbolic identification of Nineveh as a sea/nations city; not stated in Matt 12:41 and only lightly grounded in the supplied excerpts via deferred sea=peoples symbolism and the shared ‘great city’ title)
chapter_only_objections: Full scene-by-scene Passion typology of Jonah (flight/Judas, ship as nation, storm, lots, interrogation, innocent blood, casting, etc.)
Great fish as devouring ruler/Caesar-Rome and Jerusalem as spiritual Egypt delivering him
Heart of the earth as Jerusalem rather than the tomb, with the three-days count as custody in the city
Nineveh’s three days’ journey as thousand-year scale and broader gospel-to-the-nations after resurrection program
Jonah’s anger as prophecy of Israel’s envy at Gentile inclusion
strongest_counter_interpretation: Nineveh is the historical great Gentile city whose inhabitants repented at Jonah’s preaching; Jesus cites those men as exemplars of repentance who will stand up at the judgment and condemn his unrepentant generation (Matt 12:41; Luke 11:32), without redefining Nineveh as ‘a great city of the sea.’
counter_core_identification: The men of Nineveh as repentant Gentiles who will rise as condemning witnesses against the generation that rejects Jesus.
material_core_denial: None; the counter affirms the same Matt 12:41 core (repentant Gentiles who rise in judgment against rejecters) and only omits or declines the secondary ‘city of the sea’ frame.
counter_case: Matt 12:41 / Luke 11:32 function fully as a historical-exemplar contrast (repentant Ninevites vs. unrepentant hearers) without any sea-city symbolism
Jonah’s own narrative already supplies wickedness, warning, citywide repentance, and divine relenting; the Gospel citation needs no further symbolic relocation of Nineveh onto ‘the sea’
Geographically and in the Jonah narrative Nineveh is an inland Assyrian capital, not a maritime city; ‘of the sea’ is an imported symbolic gloss
Canonical dual portrait (Jonah mercy / Nahum judgment) is adequately handled by ordinary historical-theological reading without the book’s sea dictionary
book_explanatory_advantages: Keeps the entry tightly anchored to the exact wording and function of the only printed reference (Matt 12:41: repent + rise/anastēsontai in judgment + condemn)
Integrates Nineveh into the chapter’s stated sign logic: after the prophet is given back from death, the great Gentile mass turns, then rises to judge the rejecters
Uses the repeated Jonah title ‘that great city’ and the nations-turn sequence as coherent support for treating Nineveh as the representative Gentile people in the sign
counter_explanatory_advantages: Fewer unsupported moves: no need to establish sea=peoples or relocate inland Nineveh as a ‘city of the sea’
Matches the dominant catechetical use of the Ninevites as repentance exemplars who shame unbelief
Leaves room for the equally canonical Nahum/Zephaniah judgment portrait without forcing a single symbolic label
decisive_sources: Matthew 12:41 (men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment… because they repented… greater than Jonas is here)
Luke parallel usage summarized in the chapter (Jonah a sign to the Ninevites; repentance contrast)
Jonah 3 repentance sequence as the narrative basis Jesus cites
unresolved_objections: Whether ‘city of the sea’ can be sustained for Nineveh without the deferred full Sea & Waters proof
How far the glossary label should absorb Nahum’s irreversible-judgment portrait, which the short entry does not address
